key_insight: LLaMA3.3-70B achieved the highest overall chart-abstraction accuracy at 94.8%, with prompting benefits varying by clinical variable.
clinical_relevance: Locally deployed LLMs could help scale retrospective stroke registry curation and quality monitoring, with expert oversight for ambiguous cases.
method: Extracted eight clinical variables from 2,416 acute stroke intervention reports across three hospitals.
Compared 22 instruction-tuned open-source LLMs using Quick Response and Chain-of-Thought prompting.
Measured accuracy and latency against non-expert annotations, with expert review of selected discordant cases.
evidence_signal: Evaluation included only report-variable pairs with valid LLaMA3.3-70B Chain-of-Thought predictions and reference labels; two senior physicians and four medical students reviewed 20 discordant cases per variable.
watch_item: Prediction-based inclusion and selective expert review limit interpretation of overall performance; intracranial angioplasty extraction remained challenging.
paper_title: Large Language Models for Accurate Medical Chart Abstraction: Enabling Scalable and Secure Artificial Intelligence Deployment in Stroke
